slides.title: The Generalization Dilemma ⚖️
slides.content:
# Underfitting vs Overfitting

The central challenge in machine learning is ensuring a model performs well on *unseen test data*, not merely memorizing the training set.

| Diagnostic Property | High Bias (Underfitting) | Optimal Balance | High Variance (Overfitting) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Model Complexity** | Overly simplistic (e.g. linear model on non-linear curve) | Well-matched to data manifold | Excessively complex (millions of parameters memorizing noise) |
| **Training Error** | High | Low | Near Zero |
| **Validation / Test Error**| High | Low | High (massive generalization gap) |
| **Primary Remedy** | Increase model capacity, add polynomial features | Hyperparameter tuning | Regularization (L1/L2), Dropout, early stopping, more data |

quizData.question: A deep neural network scores 99.8% accuracy on its training set, but only 64.2% on the validation set. What is this model suffering from?
quizData.explanation: A massive discrepancy between near-perfect training performance and mediocre validation performance is the textbook symptom of high variance (overfitting).

slides.title: Fighting Overfitting: Regularization 🛡️
slides.content:
# Penalizing Model Complexity

Regularization shrinks weight magnitudes by appending a penalty term to the loss function:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{data}} + \lambda \cdot \Omega(\mathbf{w})$$

| Regularizer | Penalty $\Omega(\mathbf{w})$ | Geometric Effect on Weights | Best Used When... |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **L1 Regularization (Lasso)** | $\sum \|w_i\|$ | Drives non-essential weights to exact zeros (Sparsity) | Automatic feature selection across high-dimensional sparse inputs |
| **L2 Regularization (Ridge)** | $\sum w_i^2$ | Shrinks weights smoothly toward zero without zeroing | Features are collinear; prevents any single weight from dominating |
| **ElasticNet** | $\alpha L1 + (1-\alpha) L2$ | Combines sparsity with group feature selection | Datasets with many correlated features |

quizData.question: Which regularization technique creates sparse weight vectors by driving uninformative feature weights strictly to zero?
quizData.explanation: L1 regularization has sharp diamond-shaped contours in parameter space, causing optimal solutions to hit the axes at exact zeros.

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: K-Fold Cross-Validation 💡
slides.content:
## Never Rely on a Single Split
A single train-test split can yield misleading metrics if the test split happens to be unusually easy or difficult.

In **5-Fold Cross-Validation**, the dataset is partitioned into 5 equal subsets. The model is trained 5 distinct times, each time using a different subset as the hold-out validation set. The average score across all 5 folds provides an unbiased, robust estimate of model generalization!
